originality.rationale: A new sharp inverse boundary is given for the diagonal edge-degree-sum observable plus a known degree census, with analytic universal subcubic recovery and the exact smallest degree-four obstruction on eleven vertices. The known M-polynomial, joint degree matrix, tree valence-connectivity characterization and generic percolation component formulas are explicitly prior. A closer unpublished or obscure Zagreb-polynomial inversion may exist; no independent originality certification is asserted.
residual_risks: An equivalent sharp collision or diagonal-M-polynomial recovery criterion may occur in historical chemical-graph papers or specialized polynomial databases not indexed by the searches.
The full M-polynomial and known degree-index literature contain all ingredients to formulate the inverse; unpublished or overlooked consequences remain plausible.
Novelty and scientific relevance have received only the reported review; independent audit not performed.

value.rationale: The exact inverse question asks whether a measurable local ecological fragmentation statistic plus patch-degree information identifies junction-degree adjacency. The full subcubic recovery, one-dimensional degree-four ambiguity, and sharp minimum eleven-patch obstruction give a mathematically motivated identifiability boundary, not merely a recomputed graph invariant; no downstream theorem is required. Known broad graph polynomial identities are credited instead of renamed.
